items.name: HL · New order → email Tolu
items.what: The 2.1 solved problem: Google Sheets · Watch New Rows on Orders (up to 10 rows a run) sends Tolu one email per new order, with the customer name and total. Scheduled hourly, 7 a.m. to 9 p.m., so it costs about 720 credits a month at 10 orders a day and fits the Free plan.
build: 1 · Google Sheets › Watch New Rows: connection = the Harvest Lane business Google account (0.6); Search Method = Select by path; Spreadsheet = Harvest Lane spreadsheet; Sheet = Orders; Table contains headers = Yes; Row with headers = A1:Z1; Limit = 10. When asked where to start, choose From now on.

2 · Gmail › Send an Email: To = tolu@harvestlane.example (your own address); Subject = New order · {{1.customer_name}} · {{1.total}}; Content = New order from {{1.customer_name}}. Total: {{1.total}}. Map customer_name and total from module 1 in the mapping panel.
Scenario settings › Schedule: Every 60 minutes, advanced: run only between 07:00 and 21:00. Scheduling ON. Scenario name: HL · New order → email Tolu.
setup: Create a free Make account. In Make: Scenarios → Create a new scenario → the three-dot menu at the bottom → Import Blueprint → choose this file.
Click module 1 and create a Google Sheets connection with the Harvest Lane business Google account. Pick the spreadsheet and the Orders tab; headers are in row 1.
When Make asks where to start, choose From now on, so old orders are not emailed.
Click module 2 and create a Gmail connection with the same account. Put your own address in To.
Re-drop 1. customer_name and 1. total from the mapping panel if they show empty after import (Make loads the sheet headers once the sheet is picked).
Open the schedule (clock icon): every 60 minutes, advanced settings limited to 07:00–21:00. Remember the Free plan allows two active scenarios.
items.test: Add three rows to Orders and click Run once. The Sheets bubble shows 3 and the Gmail bubble shows 3; you get three emails, each with the right name and total. The run uses 4 credits (1 check + 3 emails). Click each bubble count to inspect bundle 2's input and output, then switch scheduling ON and check History after the next hourly run.

walk.title: Build it: new-order alerts, rebuilt in Make
walk.sample: Three test rows in Orders · Mrs Ade, Chef Tunde, Bodija Suites · with totals

steps.say: We're rebuilding the new-order alert from Track 1, this time in Make. Two bubbles, and we'll count every credit they use.
show: Scenario: HL · New order → email Tolu

steps.say: The trigger is Google Sheets, Watch New Rows, connected with the Harvest Lane business account, not a personal one.
show: Connection: Harvest Lane business Google account

steps.say: Pick the spreadsheet and the Orders tab, and tell Make the headers sit in row one, so each column gets a proper name.
Limit is the most rows taken in one run. When Make asks where to start, choose From now on, or the first run emails Tolu about every old order.
show: Where to start: From now on

steps.say: Next bubble: Gmail, Send an Email, to Tolu's address.
Map the customer name and total from the mapping panel. The number one in front tells you the value comes from module one, the Sheets trigger.
Add three rows and click Run once. Three rows become three bundles, so the email bubble runs three times. That's one credit for the check plus three for the emails.
Every check costs a credit even when nothing's there, so we choose the schedule with numbers. Hourly, seven in the morning to nine at night, is about 720 credits a month and fits the free plan.
Name the scenario clearly, switch scheduling on, and after the next hourly run, open History to see the bundles and credits.
show: Name: HL · New order → email Tolu

walk.end: Run once with your three rows, click each bubble count, and check that the run used exactly four credits.
